content.comment_body: I have a good background in programming previous [product_name] models, so I found it straightforward to program the [product_name]230. My goal is to use the cursor buttons to manually control the external lighting in my setup. I've programmed the C1 and C2 buttons, but they don’t respond or illuminate in online mode. I'm using the [article_no] version. Would appreciate any suggestions or tips. // [user_name]

I assume you’re pressing ESC together with the up (or left) button. From my experience, you might not get a response right away. Usually, I need to try ESC plus up (or left) several times before it works. Hope this helps.

I'll give that a try. It seems odd that ESC has to be held too, especially since I haven't seen much documentation about it (maybe I overlooked it). Thanks for your quick reply. I’ll test it soon and let you know how it goes.

Pressing ESC+C1 or other cursor buttons gives no result. Pressing ESC also opens the menu on the [product_name] device. I’ll continue experimenting when I have more time, likely over the weekend. If anyone else has ideas—maybe I’m not alone with this issue or use case—please share your thoughts.
Try right-clicking on the C1 block, then go to properties and simulation. Select among the available choices and test them. Hope this helps.

It was originally set as a switch, but I changed it to a momentary pushbutton as needed. I’ll need to test online again, but my laptop is currently broken and I’m waiting for a replacement. Alternatively, I could borrow the work device, but my supervisor may not approve. In simulation, the button works, but after downloading the program, the hardware function doesn’t respond or show feedback online.

Hi [user_name], please check page 85 (chapter 3.7.6) in the manual: [url] You need to reach the screen with cursor key icons to use the cursor keys. If you have a message text displayed permanently, you can use the cursor keys directly without entering that screen.

Hello [user_name], earlier replies suggest that you should carefully prepare your circuit, considering the following: 1) As noted, at least one text message must be active for proper function; 2) As mentioned, sometimes key recognition fails and repeated attempts are needed; 3) Regarding simulation on PC (and possibly in the actual circuit) – if using [product_name] cursor buttons as input, you need to adjust the standard simulation settings since these keys on the real device only send single pulses during each [product_name] cycle. In the real circuit, the button press duration can’t be extended. To handle this, immediately connect a flank recognition unit to the cursor key… Best regards, [user_name]

Thank you all for your responses! As mentioned, I needed to press the left cursor first to access the 'ESC+cursor' menu. I figured it out today—it’s straightforward but could be better explained in the [product_name] help function. I’ll add a permanent text to the display to make it easier for others who might operate the panel. Thanks again to everyone who replied!

I’m not sure I fully understand, but do you mean I can’t program the cursor button to require holding for some time? That setup works for me—holding ESC + C1 for about three seconds triggers the desired function, and the cycle time is much shorter. Apologies if I misunderstood your point. /[user_name]

Same for me—I built a circuit using the cursor keys on the [product_name], but it didn’t work reliably, even after trying all suggested solutions. It seems using cursor keys for input isn’t consistent; sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn’t. I can’t promise the operator or supervisor that it will always work in a production environment. It appears [company_name] made a significant error here. That’s unfortunate… If anyone finds a reliable solution—where it works just like in the simulation—please share.

Sometimes the issue is simply with the user in front of the display—it happened to me. The [product_name] didn’t always respond when pressing ESC + Cx because I made a mistake by not observing the display closely enough. I used some cursor keys in the circuit to toggle outputs and also set up a message text to show some parameters. When trying ESC+C1, I sometimes pressed ESC too long and entered the parameter mode, indicated by a blinking cursor that's hard to notice. Once I pressed ESC again, I left parameter mode and then succeeded. The key is to press the cursor button within one second of holding ESC; otherwise, you’ll enter parameter mode. Alternatively, enable 'protection' in the message text so displayed parameters can’t be changed and parameterization is disabled. Don’t wait too long after pressing ESC with Cx; otherwise, there’s no effect. The confusion comes when ESC has two roles: holding ESC for at least one second changes parameters, while holding ESC plus cursor triggers your application. As an engineer, you can avoid these problems by using protection, different message texts, etc. Reference to the relevant manual section attached. Hope this helps! Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered difficulties operating cursor buttons on the [product_name] ([article_no] version) for manual switching tasks. There were issues with unclear input sequences, lack of immediate feedback, and limited documentation. Button functions worked as expected in simulation, but hardware operation required additional menu navigation that wasn’t evident in the software help. Multiple users faced similar problems with reliability and usability of button inputs.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipated that cursor buttons would function right away for manual switching after programming, without the need for hidden steps or undocumented navigation. They wanted simulation results to align precisely with hardware behavior, with clear, accessible guidance within the programming software.
